questions.question:
Assertion (A): The value of (cos²A − 1) cosec²A = 1
Reason (R): 1 − sin²A = cos²A

options.a: A is true, R is false.
options.b: A is false, R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true.
options.d: Both A and R are false

questions.solution: (b) A is false, R is true. (cos²A − 1)cosec²A = (−sin²A)(1/sin²A) = −1, not 1. R is the identity sin²A + cos²A = 1 rearranged, so it is true.

questions.topic: Solids of revolution from a right triangle
questions.question:
A right angled triangle has sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm.
Statement 1: If the triangle is resolved about the side 12 cm a cylinder is formed.
Statement 2: If the triangle is resolved about the side 13 cm a double cone is formed.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, statement 2 is false.
options.d: Statement 1 is false, statement 2 is true.

questions.solution: (d) Statement 1 is false, statement 2 is true. Rotating a right triangle about a leg (12 cm) gives a cone, not a cylinder. Rotating about the hypotenuse (13 cm) gives two cones joined at their common base – a double cone.

marking_points.point: (d) — about a leg gives a cone; about the hypotenuse gives a double cone

questions.topic: Cyclic quadrilateral angles; proving a diameter
questions.question: In the given figure, ∠BAD = 65°, ∠ABD = 75°, ∠BDC = 50°. Find (i) ∠BCD, (ii) ∠ADB. Hence, show that AC is a diameter. (ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with diagonals AC and BD.)
questions.solution:
(i) ABCD is cyclic ⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − ∠BAD = 180° − 65° = 115°.
(ii) In ΔABD: ∠ADB = 180° − 65° − 75° = 40°.
Hence: ∠ADC = ∠ADB + ∠BDC = 40° + 50° = 90°. An angle of 90° at the circumference is an angle in a semicircle, so AC is a diameter. [Alternatively, in ΔBCD ∠DBC = 180° − 115° − 50° = 15°, so ∠ABC = 75° + 15° = 90°.]

marking_points.point: angle in semicircle ⇒ AC is diameter

questions.figure_desc: Circle with cyclic quadrilateral ABCD (A lower left, B lower right, C upper right, D upper left); diagonals AC and BD drawn; ∠BAD = 65° at A, ∠ABD = 75° at B, ∠BDC = 50° at D.

questions.question: A gulab jamun contains sugar syrup up to about 30% of its volume. Find approximately how much syrup would be found in 45 gulab jamuns, each shaped like a cylinder with two hemispherical ends with length 5 cm and diameter 2.8 cm.
Prove that sin A/(1 + cot A) − cos A/(1 + tan A) = sin A − cos A
questions.solution: LHS = sin A/((sin A + cos A)/sin A) − cos A/((cos A + sin A)/cos A) = sin²A/(sin A + cos A) − cos²A/(sin A + cos A) = (sin²A − cos²A)/(sin A + cos A) = (sin A + cos A)(sin A − cos A)/(sin A + cos A) = sin A − cos A = RHS.

marking_points.point: express cot A, tan A in sin/cos
simplify to sin²A/(sin A + cos A) and cos²A/(sin A + cos A)
combine to (sin²A − cos²A)/(sin A + cos A)
factorise to sin A − cos A

questions.topic: Ogive: median and count above a value
questions.question:
A life insurance agent found the following data for distribution of ages of 100 policy holders:
Ages in years: 20-25 | 25-30 | 30-35 | 35-40 | 40-45 | 45-50 | 50-55 | 55-60
Policy holders: 2 | 4 | 12 | 20 | 28 | 22 | 8 | 4
On a graph sheet draw an ogive using the given data. Take 2 cm = 5 years along one axis and 2 cm = 10 policy holders along the other axis. Use your graph to find:
a. The median age.
b. Number of policy holders whose age is above 52 years.
questions.solution:
Cumulative frequencies: 2, 6, 18, 38, 66, 88, 96, 100. Plot (25, 2), (30, 6), (35, 18), (40, 38), (45, 66), (50, 88), (55, 96), (60, 100), starting from (20, 0), and join with a smooth curve.
a. N = 100; median = N/2 = 50th value ⇒ from graph ≈ 42.5 years (interpolation gives ≈ 42.1).
b. From 52 on the age axis the curve gives ≈ 92 policy holders aged up to 52, so above 52 years ≈ 100 − 92 = 8.

Draw a histogram to represent the following data and find mode.
Pocket money in ₹: 150-250 | 250-350 | 350-450 | 450-550 | 550-650 | 650-750
No. of students: 5 | 10 | 7 | 4 | 6 | 2
questions.solution: Draw rectangles of width 100 on the class intervals with heights equal to the frequencies (kink on x-axis before 150). Modal class 250-350 (highest bar). Join the top-left corner of the highest bar to the top-left corner of the next bar and the top-right corner to the top-right corner of the previous bar; from their intersection drop a perpendicular. Mode ≈ ₹312.5 (by formula: 250 + (10 − 5)/(2 × 10 − 5 − 7) × 100 = 312.5; graph reading ≈ ₹315 in the key).

questions.question: The age of a father is equal to the square of the age of his son. The sum of the age of the father and five times the age of the son is 66 years. Find their present ages.
questions.solution: Let son's age = x years; father's = x². x² + 5x = 66 ⇒ x² + 5x − 66 = 0 ⇒ (x + 11)(x − 6) = 0 ⇒ x = 6 (x = −11 rejected, age cannot be negative). Son = 6 years, father = 36 years.

questions.topic: Dividend income and gain on selling half the shares
questions.question: Rohit invests ₹9000 in a company paying a dividend of 6% per annum. Each share has a face value of ₹100 and is purchased at ₹150. 1. What is his annual income from the dividend? 2. He sells 50% of his shares when the price rises to ₹200. What is his gain on this transaction?
questions.solution:
Number of shares = 9000/150 = 60.
1. Annual income = 60 × 100 × 6/100 = ₹360.
2. Shares sold = 50% of 60 = 30. Money received = 30 × 200 = ₹6000; cost of 30 shares = 30 × 150 = ₹4500. Gain = 6000 − 4500 = ₹1500.

questions.topic: Angles of depression of top and bottom of a lamp post
questions.question:
In the given figure, from the top of a building AB = 60 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a vertical lamp post CD are observed to be 30° and 60° respectively. Find:
(a) the horizontal distance between AB and CD.
(b) the height of the lamp post.
questions.solution:
Let DE ⊥ AB at E (DE = BC, BE = CD).
(a) In ΔABC: tan 60° = AB/BC ⇒ √3 = 60/BC ⇒ BC = 60/√3 = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m.
(b) In ΔAED: tan 30° = AE/DE ⇒ 1/√3 = AE/(20√3) ⇒ AE = 20 m. Height of lamp post CD = BE = AB − AE = 60 − 20 = 40 m.

questions.question: Prove that: sin A(1 + tan A) + cos A(1 + cot A) = cosec A + sec A
questions.solution: LHS = sin A + sin²A/cos A + cos A + cos²A/sin A = (sin A + cos A) + (sin³A + cos³A)/(sin A cos A) = (sin A + cos A) + (sin A + cos A)(1 − sin A cos A)/(sin A cos A) = (sin A + cos A)[1 + (1 − sin A cos A)/(sin A cos A)] = (sin A + cos A)/(sin A cos A) = 1/cos A + 1/sin A = sec A + cosec A = RHS.

marking_points.point: expand and write tan, cot as sin/cos
combine using sin³A + cos³A = (sin A + cos A)(1 − sin A cos A)
simplify to (sin A + cos A)/(sin A cos A) = cosec A + sec A

questions.topic: Compound inequation in R with number line
questions.question:
Solve the following inequation and write the solution set and represent it on number line.
−3(x − 7) ≥ 15 − 7x > (x + 1)/3, x ∈ R
questions.solution: Left: −3x + 21 ≥ 15 − 7x ⇒ 4x ≥ −6 ⇒ x ≥ −3/2. Right: 15 − 7x > (x + 1)/3 ⇒ 45 − 21x > x + 1 ⇒ 44 > 22x ⇒ x < 2. Solution set = {x : −3/2 ≤ x < 2, x ∈ R}. Number line: filled circle at −1.5, open circle at 2, segment between shaded.

questions.question: Given that (a³ + 3ab²)/(b³ + 3a²b) = 63/62. Using property find a : b
questions.solution: Componendo and dividendo: (a³ + 3ab² + 3a²b + b³)/(a³ + 3ab² − 3a²b − b³) = (63 + 62)/(63 − 62) ⇒ (a + b)³/(a − b)³ = 125/1 ⇒ (a + b)/(a − b) = 5. Again C&D: 2a/2b = 6/4 ⇒ a/b = 3/2. a : b = 3 : 2.

questions.topic: Loci: circle about a point and angle bisector
questions.question:
Use ruler and compasses only for the following question. All construction lines and arcs must be clearly shown.
(i) Construct a ΔABC in which BC = 6.5 cm, ∠ABC = 60° and AB = 5 cm.
(ii) Construct the locus of points at a distance of 3.5 cm from A.
(iii) Construct the locus of points equidistant from AC and BC.
(iv) Mark 2 points X and Y which are at a distance of 3.5 cm from A and also equidistant from AC and BC. Measure XY.
questions.solution:
(i) Draw BC = 6.5 cm; construct ∠ABC = 60° at B with compasses; cut BA = 5 cm; join AC.
(ii) Locus: circle with centre A and radius 3.5 cm.
(iii) Locus of points equidistant from AC and BC: the bisector of ∠ACB.
(iv) X and Y are where the bisector of ∠C cuts the circle. XY ≈ 5.1–5.2 cm (key: 5.1 cm; calculation: distance of A from the bisector ≈ 2.36 cm, XY = 2√(3.5² − 2.36²) ≈ 5.16 cm).

marking_points.point: X, Y marked and XY ≈ 5.1 cm

questions.topic: Two ships on opposite sides of a lighthouse
questions.question: A man on the top of a lighthouse observes the angle of depression of two ships on the opposite sides of the light house as 30° and 50° respectively. If the height of the lighthouse is 80 m, find the distance between the two ships. Give your answer to the nearest metre. (Draw the necessary diagram to the question)
questions.solution:
Diagram: lighthouse AB = 80 m, ships C and D on opposite sides on the ground line through B; ∠ACB = 30°, ∠ADB = 50° (alternate to the angles of depression).
In ΔABC: tan 30° = 80/BC ⇒ BC = 80√3 ≈ 138.56 m.
In ΔABD: tan 50° = 80/BD ⇒ BD = 80 cot 50° = 80 tan 40° ≈ 80 × 0.8391 ≈ 67.13 m.
Distance between ships CD = 138.56 + 67.13 ≈ 205.69 ≈ 206 m.

questions.topic: Tangents from external point, alternate segment, cyclic quadrilateral
questions.question: In the given diagram, O is the centre of the circle. PR and PT are two tangents drawn from the external point P and touching the circle at Q and S respectively. MN is a diameter of the circle. Given ∠PQM = 42° and ∠PSM = 25°. Find (i) ∠OQM (ii) ∠QNS (iii) ∠QOS (iv) ∠QMS
questions.solution:
(i) OQ ⊥ PR (radius ⊥ tangent), so ∠OQP = 90° ⇒ ∠OQM = 90° − 42° = 48°.
(ii) Alternate segment theorem: ∠QNM = ∠PQM = 42° and ∠MNS = ∠PSM = 25°. So ∠QNS = 42° + 25° = 67°.
(iii) ∠QOS = 2∠QNS = 134° (angle at centre).
(iv) QMSN is cyclic ⇒ ∠QMS = 180° − ∠QNS = 180° − 67° = 113°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O; tangent PR touches at Q and tangent PT touches at S from external point P; diameter MN with M near P; chords QM, MS, QN, NS drawn; OQ and OS dotted; ∠PQM = 42°, ∠PSM = 25°.

questions.question:
In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle and diameter RQ is produced to P. PT is a tangent at T.
(a) Prove ΔPQT ~ ΔPTR
(b) If PT = 6 cm, QR = 9 cm. Find the length of PQ
questions.solution:
(a) In ΔPQT and ΔPTR: ∠P is common; ∠PTQ = ∠PRT = ∠QRT (angle between tangent PT and chord TQ equals the angle in the alternate segment). Hence ΔPQT ~ ΔPTR (AA).
(b) PQ/PT = PT/PR ⇒ PT² = PQ × PR. Let PQ = x: 36 = x(x + 9) ⇒ x² + 9x − 36 = 0 ⇒ (x + 12)(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ PQ = 3 cm. [Key: OT = 4.5, OP = √(36 + 20.25) = 7.5, PR = 12, PQ = 36/12 = 3 cm.]
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O and horizontal diameter QR (QR = 9 cm) produced to the left to P; tangent PT = 6 cm touches the circle at T on top; TQ, TR and TO drawn.

A model of a ship is made to a scale of 1 : 200.
(a) The length of the model is 4 m. Calculate the length of the ship.
(b) The area of deck of the ship is 1,60,000 m². Find the area of the deck of the model.
(c) The volume of the model is 200 litres. Calculate the volume of the ship in m³.
questions.solution:
k = 1/200.
(a) Length of ship = 4 × 200 = 800 m.
(b) Area of model deck = 160000 × (1/200)² = 160000/40000 = 4 m².
(c) Volume of model = 200 L = 0.2 m³. Volume of ship = 0.2 × 200³ = 0.2 × 8,000,000 = 1,600,000 m³.

marking_points.point: 200 L = 0.2 m³ and volume uses k³

Sixteen cards are labelled as a, b, c, …, m, n, o, p. They are put in a box and shuffled. A boy is asked to draw a card from the box. What is the probability that the card drawn is: (i) A vowel (ii) A consonant (iii) None of the letter of the word median.
questions.solution:
n(S) = 16 (a to p).
(i) Vowels a, e, i, o ⇒ 4; P = 4/16 = 1/4.
(ii) Consonants = 12; P = 12/16 = 3/4.
(iii) Letters of 'median': m, e, d, i, a, n (6 cards); cards not among them = 10; P = 10/16 = 5/8.
